road.title: Time and days
road.description: A tall, folded person in a coat with more pockets than the law requires, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Gideon is a Clockwinder to the District and winds every clock in town by hand and is, as a result, always a little behind.

character.name: Gideon Dimwiddy
character.description: A tall, folded person in a coat with more pockets than the law requires, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Gideon is a Clockwinder to the District and winds every clock in town by hand and is, as a result, always a little behind.

npc.narrative: You reach the locanda in the pioggia, which falls lightly and without conviction. It is notte, and Gideon Dimwiddy stands sotto the tettoia with a grande ring of chiavi and one small biscotto, frowning at an orologio that has lost its lancette. Behind him the strada goes on into the buio, as roads do.
npc.native: Buonasera! Sono Gideon Dimwiddy e carico gli orologi del distretto. Io non so mai che ore sono, e spesso non so che giorno è, ma so a che ora apre la locanda. E tu, chi sei, che cosa cerchi qui di notte e che cosa pensi del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: Good evening! I am Gideon Dimwiddy and I wind the clocks of the district. I never know what time it is, and often I do not know what day it is, but I know at what time the inn opens. And you, who are you, what are you looking for here at night, and what do you think of my work?

player: Buonasera! Mi chiamo Sam, sono inglese. Cerco la locanda. Scusi, che ore sono?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start! You introduced yourself, said you are English, said you are looking for the inn, and politely asked Gideon the time, all in correct Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you asked Gideon the time correctly in Italian.
Not yet: you still need to ask Gideon what day it is today. Don't worry, it will come up again later.
Not yet: you still need to ask Gideon at what time something opens, starts or leaves. Don't worry, it will come up again later.

npc.narrative: Gideon searches his panciotto and offers you un piccolo biscotto, with the air of a man conferring a title. La pioggia drums on his cappello. Above you, l'orologio on the torre says one thing, and the one in his tasca another.
npc.native: Bravo, Sam! Una buona domanda: sono le nove, più o meno, ma il mio orologio è sempre indietro. Io non so mai che giorno è, e stasera non so a che ora apre la locanda. Che cosa vuoi sapere ancora, e che cosa pensi della pioggia?
npc.translation: Well done, Sam! A good question: it is nine o'clock, more or less, but my clock is always behind. I never know what day it is, and tonight I do not know at what time the inn opens. What else do you want to know, and what do you think of the rain?

player: La pioggia... non mi piace. Ma che giorno è oggi?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely, Sam! You told Gideon you don't like the rain and asked him what day it is, all in good Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you asked what day it is with "che giorno è oggi?".
You haven't yet asked Gideon at what time something opens, starts or leaves; Gideon will give you another chance to ask this later.

openObjectives.prompt: Ask Gideon at what time it opens, starts or leaves, using Italian.

npc.narrative: The pioggia taps on Gideon's cappello while he consults an orologio the size of a pane. It says nove, or forse dieci, ma it says so with great confidence. He holds out a biscotto, admires it, and keeps it per ora.
npc.native: Bravo, Sam, una domanda utile! Oggi è martedì, dice il mio orologio, ma il mio orologio è sempre indietro. Io non so a che ora apre la locanda, e non so a che ora arriva il pane. Che cosa vuoi sapere ancora, e che cosa pensi dei miei orologi?
npc.translation: Bravo, Sam, a useful question! Today is Tuesday, says my clock, but my clock is always behind. I don't know at what time the inn opens, and I don't know at what time the bread arrives. What else do you want to know, and what do you think of my clocks?

player: I tuoi orologi sono... strani! A che ora apre la locanda? Ho fame.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely, Sam! You gave your opinion of the clocks, asked at what time the inn opens, and said you are hungry, all in good Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you asked at what time the inn opens with "A che ora apre la locanda?".

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: A che ora apre la locanda?

npc.narrative: La pioggia taps on his cappello as Gideon produces a biscotto from a tasca, with the care of a man awarding a medaglia. Behind him, in the buio, an orologio strikes something that is not ten.
npc.native: Bravo, Sam! "A che ora apre la locanda?" è una domanda perfetta. La locanda apre alle dieci, credo, ma il mio orologio è indietro. Ecco un biscotto, perché hai fame! Che cosa mangi di solito la sera in Inghilterra?
npc.translation: Well done, Sam! "At what time does the inn open?" is a perfect question. The inn opens at ten, I think, but my clock is behind. Here is a biscuit, because you are hungry! What do you usually eat in the evening in England?

player: Grazie per il biscotto! In Inghilterra mangio... fish and chips, e pasta. Mi piace la pasta. E tu?

npc.narrative: The pioggia taps on the tetto of the locanda, which is chiusa and buio. Gideon brushes briciole from his giacca with great dignità. Somewhere nella notte an orologio strikes, un po' late, and he nods as if he had arranged it.
npc.native: Anch'io mangio la pasta, Sam, ma sempre tardi, perché carico gli orologi. Il pesce con le patatine è strano, ma mi piace l'idea! Qui la pasta è buona, ma la locanda è chiusa. Che cosa vuoi sapere del mio lavoro, e come cucini la pasta a casa?
npc.translation: I eat pasta too, Sam, but always late, because I wind the clocks. Fish with chips is strange, but I like the idea! Here the pasta is good, but the inn is closed. What do you want to know about my work, and how do you cook pasta at home?

player: Cucino la pasta con... tomato? pomodoro! A che ora mangi tu?

npc.narrative: The pioggia has thinned to a grey nebbia, and Gideon pulls his cappotto tighter. Behind him the orologio on the piazza says dieci, then, on reflection, nove. Across the way the locanda stays resolutely chiusa, and he regards it like a man who has written to someone about it.
npc.native: Pomodoro, certo! La pasta con il pomodoro è una buona idea, Sam. Io mangio sempre tardi, di solito alle undici, ma il mio orologio dice dieci. Che cosa vuoi sapere ancora del mio lavoro, e che cosa fai tu quando piove?
npc.translation: Tomato, of course! Pasta with tomato is a good idea, Sam. I always eat late, usually at eleven, but my clock says ten. What else do you want to know about my work, and what do you do when it rains?

player: Quando piove, leggo un libro a casa. Domani piove?

npc.narrative: Above the piazza the stelle are out, and Gideon regards them like a man whose ombrello has been made a fool of. He taps a large orologio, then consults the cielo instead. Behind the campanile a clock strikes something that is not quite an ora.
npc.native: Un libro a casa, bravo Sam! Domani non so se piove, ma stasera ci sono le stelle, e di solito sono un buon segno. Io scrivo lettere all'orizzonte, perché è molto disordinato, ma nessuno risponde. Che libro leggi quando piove, e che cosa vuoi sapere ancora del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: A book at home, well done, Sam! I don't know if it will rain tomorrow, but tonight there are stars, and they are usually a good sign. I write letters to the horizon, because it is very untidy, but nobody answers. What book do you read when it rains, and what else do you want to know about my work?
